Lever pricing starts at roughly $6,000 per year for small teams and climbs past $144,000 for enterprise organizations with 1,000+ employees, based on buyer-reported data through 2026. Like most mid-market ATS platforms, Lever doesn't publish its rates - you have to request a custom quote.

According to [Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/lever) (2025), the median negotiated LeverTRM contract for a 200-employee company runs about $12,240 per year. That's after pushing back on the initial quote. The list price for that same team size? $19,185 - a 36% markup that quietly disappears when buyers counter. At 500 employees, the gap balloons to 49%.

What follows is a breakdown of Lever's two plan tiers (LeverTRM and LeverTRM for Enterprise), the hidden costs that surface after you sign, and a comparison of Lever pricing against four ATS alternatives. Whether you're evaluating Lever for the first time or heading into renewal, this guide gives you the full budget picture.

> **TL;DR:**
>
> - **Pricing is opaque and headcount-based.** Lever charges on total company employees, not recruiter seats. Median negotiated cost ranges from $6,000/yr for small teams to $63,172/yr at 1,000+ employees ([Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/lever), 2025).
> - **List prices carry a 36-56% markup.** A 200-person team quoted at $19,185 routinely closes at $12,240 after a single counter. Negotiate hardest at 500+ employees, where the gap hits 49%.
> - **Hidden fees add 40-60%.** Implementation ($5K-$25K), data migration ($3K-$8K), and CRM add-ons ($5K-$10K/yr) are rarely in the initial quote.
> - **Q4 is the best negotiation window.** Buyers close 18-25% better deals in Q4 as Lever chases fiscal-year targets.
> - **Pin is a cheaper sourcing complement.** [Pin](https://www.pin.com/) starts at $100/mo for teams that want candidate sourcing alongside their ATS.

**Key facts at a glance:**

-   Median negotiated price (200 employees): $12,240/yr
-   List-to-negotiated discount: 36-56% depending on company size
-   Hidden fees add 40-60% to the base subscription
-   Best negotiation window: Q4 (saves 18-25%)
-   Two tiers: LeverTRM (mid-market) and LeverTRM Enterprise (2-3x the price)
-   Owner: Employ Inc. (PE-backed, also owns JazzHR and Jobvite)

## What Does Lever ATS Actually Cost in 2026?

According to [Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/lever) (2025), a 200-employee company pays a median of $12,240/yr for Lever after negotiation, while 500-employee companies pay $36,778 and 1,000-employee organizations pay $63,172. Based on total company headcount - not just the recruiters who log in - Lever's pricing scales across the entire organization. A 500-person company pays for all 500 employees even if only 5 recruiters actually use the platform day to day.

For a pricing-specific comparison, see [Workday Recruiting Pricing 2026: Full Cost Analysis](https://www.pin.com/blog/workday-recruiting-pricing/).

What companies are actually paying - based on verified buyer data from Vendr, [OutSail](https://www.outsail.co/post/lever-reviews---pricing-pros-cons-and-user-feedback), and [SelectSoftware Reviews](https://www.selectsoftwarereviews.com/reviews/lever):

<figure style="margin:2rem 0;padding:0;line-height:0"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="Lever Estimated Annual Cost (Median Negotiated)" style="width:100%;height:auto;display:block;border-radius:12px"></figure>

All figures are median negotiated prices - what organizations actually paid after back-and-forth with Lever's sales team. List prices run 36-56% higher depending on company size. OutSail (2025) estimates the base rate at $6-8 per employee per month (PEPM), which tracks with the Vendr numbers for companies in the 200-500 employee range.

Several things about Lever's ATS pricing model are worth knowing:

-   **No free tier.** Lever requires a paid annual contract. There's no free plan, no trial period, and no way to test the platform before committing budget.
-   **Annual contracts required.** All plans carry a minimum one-year commitment with auto-renewal clauses.
-   **Headcount-based scaling.** Your bill increases as your company grows - even if your hiring volume stays flat or drops.
-   **Negotiation is expected.** Vendr data shows the median discount from list price is 49% for 500-employee companies. If you're not negotiating, you're paying almost double what you should.

Most important number on this page: the negotiation gap. A 1,000-employee organization faces a list price of $144,228/yr. Median negotiated rate? $63,172 - a 56% discount. Signing at list price means $81,056 left on the table.

Already locked into a Lever contract without countering? Flag it for your next renewal. Come armed with quotes from Greenhouse, Workable, or Ashby.

According to Vendr, competitive displacement scenarios yield an additional 12-18% discount on top of standard negotiation savings.

Talking to our customers, the pattern is consistent: Lever's quoted price and the actual invoice rarely match. A 300-person company budgeting $18,000/yr based on a preliminary number often lands at $28,000-$32,000 once implementation, data migration, and the analytics add-on are factored in. That's not unique to Lever - it's how enterprise ATS sales work. What stands out about Lever specifically is the headcount-based model at growth-stage companies. A team that grows from 300 to 500 employees without adding a recruiter watches their Lever contract jump from roughly $18,000 to $31,000/yr automatically. Most ATS buyers expect costs to grow when they hire more. They don't expect costs to grow when non-recruiting headcount increases. Modelling that scaling curve before signing is worth the 30 minutes it takes.

## What Does Lever ATS Include? LeverTRM vs Enterprise Features

Two product tiers make up the Lever ATS lineup, both combining ATS and CRM in a single platform ([Lever](https://www.lever.co/pricing/), 2025). That bundled approach is Lever's core pitch - unlike pure applicant tracking tools, it lets recruiters manage candidate relationships alongside the hiring pipeline. Here's what each tier includes:

| Feature | LeverTRM | LeverTRM Enterprise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ATS + CRM | ✅ | ✅ |
| Unlimited Jobs & Candidates | ✅ | ✅ |
| 300+ Integrations | ✅ | ✅ |
| Career Site Builder | ✅ | ✅ |
| Nurture Campaigns | ✅ | ✅ |
| 20+ TA Metrics | ✅ | ✅ |
| Advanced Automation | ❌ | ✅ |
| Advanced Analytics | ❌ | ✅ |
| Custom API Integration | ❌ | ✅ |
| Data Warehouse Sync | ❌ | ✅ |
| AI Interview Companion | ❌ | ✅ |
| Compliance Features | ❌ | ✅ |
| Dedicated Support | ❌ | ✅ |

Between the two tiers, the biggest gap is analytics and automation. LeverTRM gives you basic metrics - 20+ reports covering pipeline and source tracking. Data warehouse sync, custom API access, and AI-powered analytics, however, are Enterprise-only. That upgrade isn't cheap. Vendr data suggests the Enterprise tier runs roughly 2-3x the base LeverTRM rate for the same headcount.

An AI Interview Companion was added to Lever in 2025, handling automated note-taking, sentiment tracking, and bias flagging during interviews ([AIM Group](https://aimgroup.com/2025/10/24/employ-inc-expands-automation-benchmarking-in-jazzhr-lever-jobvite/), 2025). Enterprise-only gating means mid-market teams on the standard plan can't access it without upgrading.

### Which Plan Should You Pick?

Growing companies under 200 employees with a small recruiting team will find LeverTRM covers the basics: ATS, CRM, nurture campaigns, and career site tools. Unlimited jobs and candidates is genuinely useful - some competitors cap these on lower tiers. The standard plan works well for organizations that primarily need to manage candidates through a structured pipeline.

Advanced reporting, API access, or compliance requirements are where Enterprise earns its price premium. Data warehouse integration for BI reporting lives behind the Enterprise gate, as do audit trails for regulated industries. Get quotes for both tiers and compare the actual dollar difference - it's significant, so confirm you actually need Enterprise features before paying for them.

## What Hidden Fees Does Lever Charge?

Lever charges six categories of hidden fees that surface after you sign: implementation ($5K-$25K), data migration ($3K-$8K), CRM/analytics add-ons ($5K-$16K/yr), API access fees, renewal increases (8-15% above new-customer rates), and auto-renewal traps. Together, they push total ownership 40-60% above the base subscription.

Getting the full number matters more in 2026, when 66% of TA leaders plan to increase their recruiting technology spend ([HR Executive](https://hrexecutive.com/recruiting-platforms-get-hr-tech-budget-priority-for-2026-plus-people-move-news/), 2025). Understanding what you will actually pay, not just the contract figure, is what keeps a budget honest under that pressure.

<figure style="margin:2rem 0;padding:0;line-height:0"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="Lever Hidden Cost Categories (Estimated Range)" style="width:100%;height:auto;display:block;border-radius:12px"></figure>

### 1\. Implementation and Onboarding

Implementation is quoted at $15,000-$25,000, but negotiated rates typically land between $5,000-$8,000 according to [Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/lever) (2025). Organizations with contracts over $40,000/yr can often negotiate implementation down to zero. Four onboarding packages are available - Self-Guided, Essential, Standard, and Premium - ranging from minimal support to full white-glove deployment. Teams that can handle configuration independently should push for the Self-Guided option and redirect the savings.

### 2\. Data Migration

Moving from another ATS? Budget $3,000-$8,000 for data migration per Vendr. This covers transferring candidate records, pipeline history, and configuration settings. Complex migrations from legacy platforms land at the higher end. Clean data exports on a competing ATS give you negotiating power to bring this down or bundle it with implementation at no extra cost.

### 3\. CRM and Advanced Feature Add-Ons

Despite Lever marketing itself as an ATS+CRM, some advanced CRM capabilities cost extra. The Daily Hire (2025) reports the CRM sourcing and nurture add-on runs $5,000-$10,000/yr. Advanced Analytics costs $18-32 per employee per year - for a 500-person company, that's $9,000-$16,000 annually on top of the base subscription. HRIS integration support for platforms like Workday and SuccessFactors adds $4,000-$6,000/yr (Vendr, 2025).

### 4\. API Access Fees

[OutSail](https://www.outsail.co/post/lever-reviews---pricing-pros-cons-and-user-feedback) (2025) flags API access as a significant hidden cost that catches buyers off guard. Custom API integration is locked behind the Enterprise tier, and even then, heavy API usage may carry additional fees. If you're building custom integrations or data pipelines, clarify API pricing before you sign anything.

### 5\. Renewal Price Increases

Standard annual increases at Lever run about 3%, which is moderate compared to some competitors. Vendr data reveals, though, that renewal rates run 8-15% higher than new customer rates. Discounts win the initial deal; then prices climb once you're locked in. Over a three-year contract, those increases compound:

-   Year 1: $25,000
-   Year 2 (at 8% increase): $27,000
-   Year 3 (at 8% increase): $29,160
-   **Total over 3 years: $81,160 vs. $75,000 at flat pricing**

Hidden cost totals $6,160 in this scenario - and the gap widens with larger contracts and steeper increase rates.

### 6\. Auto-Renewal Traps

Contracts auto-renew and require 30 days' advance written notice to cancel. According to [Trustpilot](https://www.trustpilot.com/review/lever.co) reviews, the cancellation window is sometimes buried in website terms rather than the main contract. Multiple reviewers report being renewed against their wishes after providing notice days short of the 30-day window. Mark your renewal date and set a reminder 45 days in advance. Don't rely on Lever to notify you.

When you stack implementation ($5K-$8K), data migration ($3K-$8K), CRM add-ons ($5K-$10K/yr), analytics ($9K-$16K/yr), and renewal increases, Lever's total cost of ownership can run 40-60% higher than the base subscription. A team budgeting $25,000/yr should realistically plan for $35,000-$42,000 in actual annual spend. Does your budget account for the real number, or just the contract price?

If those add-on costs feel steep for what you get, consider this: dedicated AI sourcing tools cover candidate discovery, multi-channel outreach, and interview scheduling for a fraction of a single Lever add-on. Pin's AI scans 850M+ profiles with 5x better response rates than industry averages - [**see how it compares**](https://www.pin.com/).

## How to Negotiate Your Lever Contract

Teams that bundle implementation, migration, and first-year training into one deal save $12,000-$18,000 compared to purchasing each separately ([Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/lever), 2025). Because the pricing is quote-based, every deal is open to counter-offers. Refusing to show a rate card is your opening to set the terms. Four tactics consistently cut costs:

### Negotiate in Q4

Deals closed in Q4 (October-December) receive 18-25% better pricing than Q1-Q2 deals, according to Vendr data. Year-end quotas drive urgency on Lever's sales team, and that urgency works in your favor. If your evaluation timeline is flexible, push the final signature into Q4. Even a 60-day delay from August to October can save five figures on an enterprise deal.

### Bring Competing Quotes

Pricing from at least two alternatives before entering negotiations is a standard buyer move. [Greenhouse](https://www.pin.com/blog/greenhouse-pricing/), Workable, and Ashby are the most common ATS alternatives buyers reference. You don't need to prefer those platforms - documented quotes give you concrete numbers to cite. Vendr reports that competitive displacement scenarios yield 12-18% additional discounts on average, plus concessions like free data migration and extended support worth $8,000-$15,000.

### Bundle Everything Upfront

Letting Lever sell implementation, migration, training, and the subscription as separate line items is a costly mistake. Roll them into a single discussion and push for a package discount. Vendr data shows bundled deals save $12,000-$18,000 versus purchasing each component on its own. Multi-year commitments are strong grounds to push for implementation and migration at no extra charge.

### Lock in a Price Cap

Lever's 3% standard annual increase sounds reasonable. But renewal rates run 8-15% above new-customer rates. Ask for a contractual cap - ideally 0-3% maximum annual increase - as part of your initial agreement. Multi-year commitments (2-3 years) typically unlock an additional 8-18% discount plus protection against increases (Vendr, 2025). Locking a $36,000/yr deal at 3% max increase saves over $8,000 compared to absorbing 10% annual bumps over three years.

## How Does Lever Compare to 4 ATS Alternatives?

At the mid-range of ATS pricing - more expensive than SMB-focused tools but cheaper than enterprise-only platforms - Lever occupies a specific bracket. According to The Daily Hire (2025), buyers pay a 30-50% premium for Lever's UI and CRM functionality compared to alternatives offering similar ATS features at lower price points. Here's how the platforms compare:

Entry points only - add-ons and headcount scaling push actual spend significantly higher for most organizations, particularly at Lever given its six hidden cost categories. The table below captures key platform differences at a glance:

| Platform | Starting Price | Free Tier | ATS + CRM | Pricing Model |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Workable | ~$2,028/yr | ❌ | ⚠️ Basic CRM | Per-employee, tiered |
| JazzHR | ~$3,600/yr | ❌ | ❌ ATS only | Flat monthly tiers |
| Greenhouse | ~$5,100/yr | ❌ | ⚠️ Add-on | Employee count, tiered |
| Lever | ~$6,000/yr | ❌ | ✅ Built-in | Headcount + add-ons |
| Ashby | ~$10,000/yr | ❌ | ✅ Built-in | Quote-based |

Each alternative warrants a closer look:

**JazzHR** is Lever's sibling - both are owned by Employ Inc. It targets smaller teams with transparent, flat-rate pricing starting at $300/mo. JazzHR covers basic ATS needs (job posting, applicant tracking, collaborative hiring) but doesn't include CRM, advanced automation, or the analytics depth Lever offers. Think of it as the entry-level option within the Employ family.

**Workable** is the most affordable option on this list with publicly listed pricing starting at $299/mo for up to 20 employees. It works well for smaller teams that want predictable costs without negotiating. Sourcing and reporting are limited compared to Lever, and CRM capabilities are basic rather than built-in.

**Greenhouse** starts slightly below Lever at ~$5,100/yr but uses a different pricing structure with three tiers (Core, Plus, Pro). Greenhouse is more structured-interview-focused, while Lever leans heavier into CRM and candidate relationship management. For a detailed look at Greenhouse's pricing, hidden fees, and negotiation tactics, see our [complete Greenhouse pricing breakdown](https://www.pin.com/blog/greenhouse-pricing/).

**[Ashby](/blog/ashby-pricing/)** sits above Lever at roughly $10,000/yr and is gaining traction with growth-stage companies. It bundles ATS, CRM, and analytics in one platform with a focus on recruiter productivity. Pricing is quote-based, so your actual cost depends on company size and configuration.

**Pinpoint** targets mid-market teams at around $345/mo and uses an unlimited-seat model - a 10-recruiter team pays the same as a 3-recruiter team, unlike Lever's per-employee pricing. For teams where recruiter headcount matters, that's a meaningful cost advantage. See our [Pinpoint pricing breakdown](/blog/pinpoint-pricing/) for full tier and hidden-cost details.

Notably absent from every ATS on this list: deep AI-powered candidate sourcing. These platforms manage applicants who find you - not candidates who haven't applied yet. That's a different category, and it's where the cost equation shifts for organizations whose pipeline depends on proactive outreach. For teams exploring recruitment automation beyond traditional ATS, the market has expanded significantly.

## Who Owns Lever? Why It Matters for Pricing

Lever is owned by Employ Inc., a private-equity-backed holding company that also owns JazzHR, Jobvite, and NXTThing RPO. Who owns the company matters because it directly shapes how Lever pricing decisions get made, and who those decisions benefit.

K1 Investment Management, a private equity firm, acquired Lever for Employ in August 2022 ([BusinessWire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20220805005292/en/Lever-Joins-Employ-to-Accelerate-Growth), 2022). This corporate structure affects your pricing experience in several practical ways.

Employ segments its portfolio by company size. JazzHR targets SMBs. Mid-market is Lever's segment. Jobvite targets enterprise. Outgrowing Lever means the natural upsell path is [Jobvite](/blog/jobvite-pricing/) - at a significantly higher price point. Coming in under Lever's size threshold means sales may steer you toward JazzHR instead. Understanding this segmentation helps you gauge whether you're being quoted appropriately or pushed toward a tier designed to maximize Employ's revenue per customer.

PE-backed companies operate under financial targets that prioritize margin growth. [TechTarget](https://www.techtarget.com/searchhrsoftware/news/252523781/Cobbling-together-a-recruiting-software-empire) described Employ's approach as "cobbling together a recruiting software empire." For buyers, this can mean add-on upsells that serve the portfolio's revenue goals more than your team's actual needs.

Worth watching closely: [Trustpilot](https://www.trustpilot.com/review/lever.co) reviews include reports of Lever responding to product bug complaints - bot applications, broken LinkedIn integration, search failures - by upselling paid add-ons rather than fixing core issues. That dynamic, where fixes come as paid upgrades, is more common in PE-owned software than founder-led companies. It doesn't mean Lever is a bad product. But it does mean you should scrutinize whether an "add-on" solves a genuine new need or patches a gap that should be covered in your existing subscription.

Employ appointed a new CEO (Jerry Jao) and CTO (Patrick Jean) in February 2026, both with mandates to accelerate AI innovation ([GlobeNewsWire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/02/18/3240112/0/en/Employ-Inc-Appoints-Jerry-Jao-as-CEO.html), 2026). Pricing changes may follow, since leadership transitions at PE-backed companies often precede restructures - though the timeline remains unclear. If you're signing a multi-year Lever deal in 2026, negotiate pricing protection clauses upfront.

## What If Sourcing Is Your Real Bottleneck?

Seventy-nine percent of organizations have already integrated AI into their recruiting processes ([Select Software Reviews](https://www.selectsoftwarereviews.com/blog/applicant-tracking-system-statistics), 2026), yet most ATS platforms remain applicant-management tools - they track candidates who apply, not candidates who haven't. When the pipeline bottleneck is finding qualified talent, dedicated AI sourcing tools deliver better ROI than ATS sourcing add-ons at a fraction of the cost. [SHRM](https://www.shrm.org/topics-tools/news/talent-acquisition) reports that recruitment remains the top staffing challenge for HR professionals heading into 2026.

Organizing resumes, scheduling interviews, and moving candidates through pipeline stages is what an ATS does. Lever does this well, and its CRM adds relationship-tracking on top.

Sourcing is a different problem entirely.

Finding qualified candidates who haven't applied and may not know your role exists requires a different tool - one built for outbound discovery, not inbound tracking.

Based on Pin's data, this gap is wider than most teams assume. Across 80,000+ candidate outreach interactions Pin tracked in 2025, 59% of replies came from a follow-up message, not the first one. Software that waits for applicants never sends those follow-ups, so it reaches less than half the talent a structured sequence would. Inbound-only tracking quietly leaves that pipeline on the table.

When the pipeline bottleneck is finding the right people, the cost math shifts dramatically for recruiting teams and agencies. Spending $25,000-$60,000/yr on an ATS with add-ons may not deliver the best return when dedicated AI sourcing tools exist at a fraction of that price.

[Pin's AI sourcing](https://www.pin.com/) gives recruiters access to 850M+ candidate profiles with automated outreach across email, LinkedIn, and SMS. Pin users see 5x better response rates on outreach and fill positions in an average of 14 days - the fastest time-to-fill of any AI recruiting platform. That's the sourcing side handled for $100-$249/mo, less than what many teams spend on a single Lever add-on.

As Nick Poloni, President at Cascadia Search Group, put it: "I jumped into Pin solo toward the end of 2025 and closed out the year with over $1M in billings during just the final 4 months - no team, no agency. The sourcing data is incredible, scanning 850M+ profiles with recruiter-level precision to uncover perfect-fit candidates I'd never find otherwise."

Side-by-side, the investment comparison looks like this:

| Capability | Lever (with Add-Ons) | Pin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Annual Cost (single recruiter) | $6,000+/yr (base only) | $1,200/yr ($100/mo) |
| Candidate Database | Internal + integrations | 850M+ profiles |
| Multi-Channel Outreach | ⚠️ Email (add-on required) | ✅ Email, LinkedIn, SMS |
| Outreach Response Rate | Not disclosed | 5x industry average |
| AI-Powered Search | ⚠️ Basic (Enterprise only) | ✅ Advanced AI matching |
| Interview Scheduling | ✅ (via ATS) | ✅ Built-in |
| Free Tier | ❌ | ✅ |
| SOC 2 Certified | ✅ | ✅ |

Skipping an ATS entirely isn't the takeaway here. Combined applicant tracking and CRM for structured workflows is where Lever earns its position. But when sourcing is the pipeline bottleneck, Pin is the best option for recruiting teams: 850M+ candidate profiles, 5x better outreach response rates, and an average of 14 days to fill. At $100-$249/mo, that's less than one Lever add-on. Many teams run both - a lightweight ATS for tracking plus Pin for sourcing - at a lower combined cost per hire than Lever with all its add-ons.

## Lever ATS Review: Features, Pricing, Pros and Cons

Buyers consistently give Lever ATS positive marks for its CRM and nurture campaign tools. Pipeline visualization ranks among the stronger implementations in the mid-market ATS category, based on reviews aggregated across [G2](https://www.g2.com/products/lever/reviews) and Capterra (2025). Recurring criticisms center on implementation timelines exceeding sales estimates, enterprise tier pricing surprises, and support quality dropping post-onboarding.

### Where Lever ATS Earns Praise

CRM and candidate relationship management features draw genuine praise - organizations actively using nurture campaigns and talent pools report stronger pipeline visibility. Unlimited jobs and candidates (no per-role caps) earns positive marks compared to competitors that cap volume on lower tiers. Buyers transitioning from spreadsheets or basic ATS tools consistently highlight the improvement in collaborative review workflows and pipeline organization.

### Where Buyers Push Back

Recurring buyer criticisms cover three areas. Implementation takes longer than sales represents. The Enterprise tier adds significant cost for features buyers assumed were standard. The headcount-based model penalizes growing organizations even when hiring volume stays flat. [Trustpilot](https://www.trustpilot.com/review/lever.co) reviewers specifically flag support responsiveness dropping after the onboarding period ends. For sourcing-focused teams, the structural gap remains: applicant tracking is what Lever ATS handles - proactive candidate discovery is a different problem entirely.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How Much Does Lever ATS Cost in 2026?

Lever ATS pricing in 2026 ranges from approximately $6,000/yr for small teams to $63,000-$144,000+/yr for enterprise organizations with 1,000+ employees, based on buyer-reported data from [Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/lever) (2025). The median negotiated contract for a 200-employee company is about $12,240/yr. Exact pricing requires a custom quote since Lever doesn't publish rates publicly.

### How much does Lever cost for recruiting teams?

Total company headcount drives the bill, not recruiter seats. Even a five-recruiter team at a 500-person company pays for all 500 employees, roughly $36,778/yr at the median negotiated rate ([Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/lever), 2025). Smaller teams that need only a handful of recruiter logins often pay less with a seat-based or flat-rate ATS. If sourcing is the real priority, an AI sourcing platform like Pin starts at $100/mo and scans 850M+ profiles regardless of company size.

### Does Lever offer a free plan or free trial?

No. Lever doesn't offer a free tier or free trial. Annual contracts with auto-renewal are required for all plans. Testing recruiting software before committing budget is still possible - AI sourcing platforms like Pin offer free tiers with no credit card required, so you can evaluate sourcing quality before signing a long-term deal.

### Is Lever cheaper than Greenhouse?

Lever's starting price (~$6,000/yr) is slightly higher than Greenhouse's (~$5,100/yr), but total cost depends heavily on add-ons and company size. For a detailed comparison, see our [Greenhouse pricing breakdown](https://www.pin.com/blog/greenhouse-pricing/). Both platforms charge extra for sourcing, advanced analytics, and premium support. Neither publishes pricing publicly, so always negotiate.

### Who owns Lever?

Employ Inc. owns Lever - a private-equity-backed holding company also behind JazzHR, Jobvite, and NXTThing RPO. K1 Investment Management acquired Lever in August 2022. Employ serves 26,000+ customers across its portfolio and appointed new leadership (CEO Jerry Jao, CTO Patrick Jean) in February 2026 with a mandate to accelerate AI innovation.

### What are the best alternatives to Lever for AI-powered sourcing?

Lever is an ATS/CRM, not an AI sourcing tool. For AI-powered candidate sourcing, dedicated platforms search 850M+ profiles and automate outreach across email, LinkedIn, and SMS starting at $100/mo. Many recruiting teams pair a lightweight ATS with an AI sourcing tool for better results at lower total cost. For more options, see our guide to [LinkedIn Recruiter alternatives](https://www.pin.com/blog/linkedin-recruiter-alternatives-2026/).

## Should You Buy Lever in 2026?

As an ATS+CRM, Lever is a capable tool with rates that reflect its mid-market positioning. Small teams start around $6,000/yr. Mid-market organizations pay $12,000-$37,000/yr. Enterprise deployments can hit $63,000-$144,000+. Factor in implementation, analytics, CRM add-ons, and renewal increases, and the real spend runs 40-60% above the contract number.

To put Lever pricing in perspective: a 200-employee company running the platform with standard add-ons (analytics, CRM sourcing, HRIS integration) for three years pays approximately $75,000-$95,000 all-in. A lightweight ATS plus a dedicated AI sourcing tool for the same organization over three years runs roughly $25,000-$40,000 - and covers both tracking and proactive candidate discovery.

Before signing, map your actual hiring bottleneck. Combined applicant tracking and candidate relationship management for structured workflows is where Lever delivers - its CRM functionality genuinely differentiates it from ATS-only tools. When the gap is on the sourcing side, Pin is the best alternative: start free, search 850M+ candidate profiles, and fill positions in an average of 14 days without the enterprise price tag.
